researched_by: secondary sources reporting the Trust's stated policy
policy_summary:
A single national policy: no overnight parking in National Trust car parks, which the Trust attributes to litter, fires and human waste. That covers thousands of car parks, many in exactly the coastal and upland places vans want to be.

NUANCE, from staff conversations reported by visitors: leaving a VEHICLE overnight in a Trust car park is often treated as acceptable; it is overnight OCCUPATION that is objected to. So the practical position may be the parking-versus-sleeping split again rather than a flat ban on presence. Not confirmed from the Trust's own wording, and it would not be safe to rely on.
notes: A blanket no is still valuable data. Knowing the National Trust is never an option removes a large number of tempting-looking car parks from consideration, which is worth as much to a user as finding a yes.
open_questions: Find the Trust's own published wording. Everything here is second-hand, and the parking-versus-sleeping distinction changes the answer materially.
Find the Trust's own published statement rather than forum reporting.
Are there any exceptions - member events, campsite-adjacent car parks, Trust-run campsites?
Does National Trust for Scotland have the same policy?

RESOLVED IN PART by the 2026-07-27 sweep: the exceptions question. The Trust does run campsites and caravan parks, twelve of them recorded here, and does take motorhomes and campervans on booked pitches. The car park prohibition and the campsite business coexist.

STILL OPEN: the Trust's own published wording on overnight parking in car parks. The sweep looked at the holidays side of the site, not the parking side, and found nothing that states the car park rule in the Trust's own words.

No campsite price is published anywhere on nationaltrust.org.uk - every page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk and prices only appear after choosing dates. Somebody should sample the booking engine for a typical motorhome pitch price at three or four sites.

Hoathwaite (Torver, Coniston) is described by third-party listings as a National Trust campsite but has no page under /holidays/ that could be found, and did not appear in the Trust's own campsite lists. Open or closed in 2026, and does it take vehicles?

Upper Booth Farm at Edale in the Peak District and Heber Farm at Buckden in Wharfedale are listed by third parties as National Trust campsites. Both look like tenant-farm businesses on Trust land rather than Trust-run sites, and neither appears in the Trust's own campsite list. Confirm the tenure and, if they are Trust-owned, record them here with the operator named.

Dolaucothi in Carmarthenshire is listed by third parties as a caravan and motorhome park on National Trust land. No page for it could be found on nationaltrust.org.uk and the property page 404s. Whether it is Trust-run, club-run on Trust land, or closed is unresolved - and it is the one site in this sweep most likely to be the Wansbeck/Ballater pattern.

Are there Camping and Caravanning Club or Caravan and Motorhome Club sites sitting on National Trust freehold elsewhere? The scope rule says those belong in this file with the operator named, and none was confirmed either way.

sites.name: All National Trust car parks
sites.notes: Stated national policy of no overnight parking, though reported practice suggests the objection is to sleeping rather than to leaving a vehicle. Not law - a condition of entry - so no penalty charge notice, but they can require you to leave. NEEDS the Trust's own published wording, which has not yet been found.

sites.name: National Trust campsites and caravan parks - network
sites.notes:
This answers the open question the first pass could not: yes, there are exceptions, and they are a business rather than a courtesy. The Trust runs its own campsites and caravan parks, takes motorhomes and campervans at most of them, and sells the pitches through its own booking engine at camping.nationaltrust.org.uk. None of this is reachable from anything about car parks - it lives under /holidays/, a different department and a different part of the site, exactly the blind spot the research protocol warns about.

The two policies are not in conflict. The Trust's position is that you may not sleep in a vehicle in a Trust car park, and that you may sleep in a vehicle on a Trust pitch you have booked and paid for. A van user reading only the car park rule would conclude the Trust is never an option, and would be wrong.

Eleven sites take motorhomes or campervans and are recorded individually below: Weston Farm (Dorset), Low Wray, Great Langdale, Wasdale and Eskdale (Lake District), Highertown Farm and Teneriffe Farm (Cornwall), Cloud Farm (Exmoor), Waterclose Meadows (Cambridgeshire), Gupton Farm (Pembrokeshire) and Castle Ward Caravan Park (County Down). Brownsea Island (shepherd's huts, boat access), Watkin Bunkhouse and West Challacombe Bothy are Trust accommodation but not vehicle provision and are not recorded.

The operating pattern is consistent: the Trust is named as operator on every one of these pages, including the ones with farm names, which are Trust-owned holdings rather than tenant businesses. Vehicle length is the recurring constraint - 6m at Highertown and Cloud Farm hardstanding, 6.5m at Wasdale, Eskdale and Great Langdale, 8m at Waterclose Meadows - and caravans are refused outright at Wasdale, Great Langdale, Low Wray, Cloud Farm and Gupton Farm because of the approach roads. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.

sites.name: Weston Farm Motorhome Site, Worth Matravers, Dorset
sites.self_contained_definition: the Trust accepts 'motorhomes and campervans with onboard toilets only'
sites.notes: The find of this sweep. A five-pitch, motorhome-and-campervan-only site on the Purbeck coast, hardstanding with hook-up and chemical disposal, open all year (1 January to 31 December 2026), minimum one night, self-contained required. That is an aire in everything but name, run by the organisation whose published position is that you cannot sleep in its car parks. Sea views over Chapman's Pool, ten minutes' walk from Worth Matravers, on the grounds of an old dairy farm on Renscombe Road. Free entry to Corfe Castle and Brownsea Island during the stay. Raised gas BBQs allowed, no campfires, two dogs per pitch. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.

sites.name: Low Wray Campsite, Windermere
sites.notes: Hardstanding campervan and motorhome pitches, most with electric hook-up, on the western shore of Windermere. 129 units of accommodation of all types. Open 13 February to 1 November 2026, minimum two nights and three over bank holidays, check-in 15:00, away by 11:00. Caravans of any length are refused and the approach road is narrow, which the Trust warns larger motorhomes about explicitly. No lakeside pitches for vehicles - those are for tents. Maximum four adults in a group. Quiet 22:00 to 07:00. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid at Low Wray; the campsite runs down to the Windermere shore south of the postcode point, so the pin is within a few hundred metres of the pitches rather than on them

sites.name: Great Langdale Campsite
sites.notes: Hardstanding pitches with electric hook-up for campervans and motorhomes up to 6.5m, beneath the Langdale Pikes. 175 pitches in total, 120 of them tent pitches, plus nine pods. Open essentially all year (27 December 2025 to 31 December 2026), minimum two nights, check-in from noon, away by 11:00. No caravans of any size. Campfires allowed if raised, EV charging on site. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid at the head of Great Langdale; the postcode covers the campsite and the Old Dungeon Ghyll area, single-source

sites.name: Wasdale Campsite, Wasdale Head
sites.notes: Campervans under 6.5m and motorhomes accepted with electric hook-up; caravans are refused because of the access road. 120 pitches of all types at the foot of Scafell Pike, a mile from Wast Water. Open all year except 24 to 26 December. Minimum two nights, check-in 14:00, away by 10:00. EV charging shared. A 2026 notice restricted road access 22:00 to 06:00 for infrastructure works, which is the sort of thing worth re-checking before travelling. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid at Wasdale Head; the campsite sits a little south-west of the postcode point at the head of Wast Water, single-source

sites.name: Eskdale Campsite, Boot
sites.notes: Electric and non-electric pitches in the main field for campervans and motorhomes up to 6.5m, eight acres at the foot of Hardknott Pass. 110 pitches. Open 13 February to 31 December 2026 except 24 to 26 December, minimum two nights, check-in 14:00, away by 10:00. Maximum four adults in any booking, which the Trust states is deliberate. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid at Boot in Eskdale; single-source and the postcode unit is large, so treat the pin as the valley location rather than the entrance

sites.name: Highertown Farm Campsite, Lansallos, Cornwall
sites.notes: Campervans and motorhomes up to 6m on grass - there is no hardstanding, which in a Cornish spring is the constraint that matters. 30 pitches, electric hook-ups available, near the South West Coast Path and Lansallos Cove. Open 27 March to 31 October 2026, minimum one night, check-in 13:00, away by 11:00. Unmanned site with ranger support, so nobody is on the gate. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid at Lansallos; single-source

sites.name: Teneriffe Farm Campsite, Predannack, Cornwall
sites.notes: Grass pitches for campervans, motorhomes, trailer tents and - unusually for the Trust - touring caravans, on the Lizard peninsula. 20 pitches in low season rising to 60 in high season. Open 27 March to 31 October 2026, minimum one night, check-in 14:00, away by 11:00. Electric hook-up, shop, wifi, dog wash. No published length limit, which given the lanes is worth confirming before taking anything long. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid at Predannack on the Lizard; single-source

sites.name: Cloud Farm Campsite, Oare, Exmoor
sites.notes: Hardstanding pitches with electric hook-up for vehicles up to 6m, grass pitches without electricity up to 5.5m, 58 pitches beside the river in the Lorna Doone valley. Caravans refused on access grounds. Open 27 March to 1 November 2026, minimum one night, check-in 13:30, away by 11:00. Campfires allowed, EV charging shared, wifi. Geographically this is inside Exmoor National Park but it is National Trust land and a National Trust business, so it belongs here and not in the Exmoor National Park Authority file. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.
sites.geocode_precision: campsite address postcode centroid in the Lorna Doone valley at Oare; single-source

sites.name: Waterclose Meadows Campsite, Houghton Mill, Cambridgeshire
sites.notes: All-grass site, no hardstanding, taking campervans, motorhomes and caravans up to 8m - the most generous length limit in the Trust's network. 51 pitches beside the Great Ouse at the 18th-century working watermill. Open 2 March 2026 to 3 January 2027 except 24 to 26 December, minimum one night, check-in 13:00, away by noon. Electric hook-up and chemical disposal. Free entry to the mill during a stay. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.

sites.name: Castle Ward Caravan Park, Strangford, County Down
sites.notes: The Trust's only Northern Ireland vehicle site found in this sweep, and the most fully equipped one anywhere in its network: 25 hardstanding pitches for caravans, campervans and motorhomes, every one with electric AND water hook-up. Ten grass tent pitches and pods as well. Open all year except 24 to 26 December, minimum one night, check-in 14:00, away by noon. Chemical disposal, laundry, dog shower with ramp, accessible toilets showers and laundry. On the shore of Strangford Lough, a short walk from Strangford village. Note this is in Northern Ireland while the file's nation field says England - the National Trust covers England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and the separate National Trust for Scotland file is a different organisation. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.

sites.name: Gupton Farm Campsite, Castlemartin, Pembrokeshire
sites.notes: Twenty campervan pitches behind Freshwater West: five with electric hook-up (four grass, one hardstanding) and fifteen without. Caravans and trailer tents refused because of the pitch sizes and the access route. Open 4 March to 1 November 2026, check-in 14:00, away by 11:00. Bring levelling blocks - the Trust says the pitches may not be flat. NOT MAPPED, deliberately: the Trust publishes no postcode for Gupton Farm and warns in terms that a postcode 'will not bring you to the right location', giving what3words ///tango.century.even instead. No coordinate is recorded here rather than a guessed one. Prices are not published on the Trust's site pages at all - every campsite page routes to camping.nationaltrust.org.uk for rates, so no price is recorded here rather than guessed.

provision_sweep_2026_07_27: Gap-filling sweep for provision the car park pages do not mention (research protocol step 2). Result: large, and it changes the file's headline. The National Trust runs its own campsites and caravan parks under /holidays/, sells pitches through camping.nationaltrust.org.uk, and takes motorhomes and campervans at eleven of the twelve vehicle-capable sites found. Weston Farm in Dorset is a five-pitch motorhome-only aire in all but name. The blanket 'no overnight in Trust car parks' record is untouched and still stands - the two things are separate regimes. Coordinates here are address postcode centroids from postcodes.io; none is corroborated against a second geocode source, so they are all banded approximate. Gupton Farm is deliberately unmapped because the Trust publishes no usable postcode for it. Note also that National Trust for Scotland is a different organisation with its own file.
